original_question: Find the exact value of Dhat_conv(n), where Dhat_conv(n) is the largest number such that every set of n points in strict convex position contains a point whose distances to the other n-1 points realize at least Dhat_conv(n) distinct values.
target_in_paper: Section 3 on restricted/constrained planar point sets, specifically the open problem asking for the exact value of \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n): this appears as Problem 7 in the current arXiv HTML rendering, and as Problem 10 in an accessible PDF draft of the same survey section after the definitions of D_{conv}(n) and \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1406.1949))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right local parameter \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n), the universal quantifier over all n-point sets in convex position, and the existential conclusion that some point determines at least that many distinct distances to the other n-1 points. That is exactly the quantity the paper defines immediately before posing the corresponding open problem. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: this section of the paper is planar, so the point sets lie in R^2. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

The paper’s restriction is “n points in (strict) convex position”; using that exact phrase keeps the question aligned with the survey’s formulation. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
The metric should be made explicit: the distances are Euclidean distances, written in the surrounding literature as |pq|. ([math.nyu.edu](https://math.nyu.edu/~pach/publications/distdist042512.pdf))

The quantifiers should be spelled out fully: for every set P of n points in convex position, there exists p in P such that the distances from p to the other points of P realize at least \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) distinct values. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to distinguish the local one-vertex parameter \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) from the global parameter D_{conv}(n), since the paper defines both side by side. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))

If you want the question to mirror the paper’s nearby context, you may also mention that the paper records the upper bound \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) ≤ floor(n/2), the lower bounds inherited from no-three-collinear sets and Dumitrescu/Nivasch–Pach–Pinchasi–Zerbib, and Erdős’s conjectured exact value floor(n/2); these are contextual rather than strictly part of the bare problem statement. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
refined_question: For each integer n ≥ 2, let \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) denote the largest integer with the following property: every set P ⊂ R^2 of n points in (strict) convex position contains a point p ∈ P such that the Euclidean distances {|pq| : q ∈ P, q ≠ p} take at least \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) distinct values. Determine the exact value of \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n). ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
justification: The closest official formulation in arXiv:1406.1949 is not a numbered conjecture but the Section 3 open problem asking for the exact value of \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n). In the same nearby passage, the survey defines D_{conv}(n) and \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n), notes the regular n-gon upper bound \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n) ≤ floor(n/2), records Erdős’s stronger conjecture \widehat{D}_{\mathrm{conv}}(n)=floor(n/2), and recalls the best known lower bounds before posing the exact-value problem. Your draft is therefore already very close to the paper’s intent; it mainly needed the ambient space, metric, and the paper’s exact quantifier package to become fully self-contained. ([adamsheffer.wordpress.com](https://adamsheffer.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/06/distprobs3.pdf))
